items.reason: TarGeT-A entry requires 'at least one relevant actionable somatic alteration', listed under 'Pathogenic alterations presumed to cause activation of the PI3K/mTOR pathway' including 'Deletion or mutation of TSC1 or TSC2'; §5 asks for one row per biomarker, and TSC1/2 is mechanistically linked to the mTOR inhibitor everolimus. items.coder_A: ["other", true, "ribociclib"] (RB1 homozygous loss, enrichment, Strata A-D)
items.proposed: Keep A's row: other = RB1 homozygous loss (excluded), enrichment (Strata A-D), candidate_matched true, matched_agent ribociclib
items.reason: 'Patients with evidence of homozygous (biallelic) RB1 loss by sequencing are excluded from TarGeT-A' makes RB1-intact status an entry condition for the ribociclib strata, and RB1 is the downstream target of CDK4/6 inhibition. The manual does not say explicitly whether a biomarker used as an exclusion counts as selection, so this is a reading, not a rule.

note: Primary outcome is true on the agreed CDK4_6_pathway, CDKN2A_B and PTEN_PI3K rows regardless of the two A-only rows; it is subject to the D21(a) review of positive matches. Priority-3 role difference (eligibility in B vs enrichment in A for the Strata A-D requirement) does not change the outcome; enrichment fits better because Stratum E does not require these alterations. Ribociclib is the only investigational agent in Stratum E (temozolomide backbone), noted by both coders. Paediatric/young adult trial (mixed_age).
